categories_checked.note: Study grants are a Community competence: Flemish studietoelage (Flanders + Dutch-language institutions in Brussels, e.g. VUB) and FWB allocations d'études (Wallonia + French-language institutions in Brussels). Both require prior residence/work links for EU and non-EU students.

No general student rent allowance found at regional level. Only university measures: UCLouvain rent reduction for its own housing; UGent gives housing priority (no rent reduction); VUB social housing (SVKS) prices in the Brussels city file.

No student-specific health subsidy found. EU students with an EHIC register at a fund without contribution (rule, see bureaucracy.json). The increased-reimbursement status (BIM / verhoogde tegemoetkoming) exists but its student conditions were not researched.
De Lijn Buzzy Pazz Jongere (18-24) and STIB 18-24 Bruxellois annual pass. TEC (Wallonia, Louvain-la-Neuve) could not be read: letec.be refused automated access.
Jobstudent tax-free threshold 2026 (Flemish government page). Parents' dependent-child allowance not researched in detail.
Reduced social contributions within the 650-hour Student@work quota. The exact rate (2.71% student share per secondary sources) was not on an official page we could read.

No host-side top-up for incoming Erasmus students found at Flemish, FWB or university level (incoming students are paid by their home country). Found only outgoing measures for UGent students (exchange allowance) and the rule that FWB grants still count an Erasmus stay. Master Mind cannot be combined with Erasmus+.
Flemish Master Mind scholarship; Flemish Groeipakket (child benefit) for students. Wallonia (AVIQ/FAMIWAL) and Brussels (Iriscare) family allowances were not researched.
KU Leuven Stuvo, UGent social services and reduced tuition, VUB interest-free loan and reduced tuition, UCLouvain tuition reduction and support for non-EU students.

items.name_it: Borsa di studio fiamminga per l'istruzione superiore
items.authority: Flemish Government, Studietoelagen department (Flemish Community: Flanders and Dutch-language institutions in Brussels)
items.description: Means-tested yearly grant for students at Flemish higher education institutions; it also gives the reduced 'beurstarief' tuition. From 2026-2027 you must be under 30 on 31 December and, with exceptions, take at least 54 credits.

eligibility.income_test: Household income (and in some cases cadastral income) below the limits
eligibility.residence_requirement: On 31 December of the academic year: EU national with 5 years' continuous residence in Belgium; or EEA national who (or whose parent) worked in Belgium at least 12 months in the last 2 years with a contract of at least 32 hours/month, or was self-employed 2 years; or holder of a permanent residence card (or 5 years with an E/EU card); non-EU: 12 months' lawful residence on a permit NOT granted for study or work, or recognised refugee/subsidiary protection
eligibility.min_work_hours: 32 hours/month for 12 months within 2 years (EEA route via work)
other: Enrolled in a Flemish (Dutch-language) institution, including VUB in Brussels
At least 54 credits from 2026-2027 unless an exception applies (final year, working student, no Dutch secondary diploma enrolling for the first time, etc.)

items.amount: 2026-2027 (60 credits): minimum € 343.20; full grant € 5,311.19 living away from home (kot) / € 3,187.74 living at home; exceptional grant € 7,150.80 / € 4,625.87
items.how_to_apply: Online via the Digitaal loket Studietoelagen; one application also checks reduced tuition
items.deadline: From 2 June 2026 to 1 June 2027 for academic year 2026-2027
items.stackable: Grant holders automatically pay the reduced scholarship tuition rate at their Flemish institution; university social services build on it (advances, allowances)
items.notes: In practice a student who moves to Belgium only to study does not qualify (a residence permit granted for study does not count). Swiss nationals are not mentioned explicitly on the nationality page.

items.name_it: Assegno di studio della Federazione Vallonia-Bruxelles
items.authority: Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, Direction des Allocations d'Études (French Community: Wallonia and French-language institutions in Brussels)
items.description: Means-tested grant for full-time students in French-speaking higher education; grant holders also pay no tuition (minerval € 0).

eligibility.income_test: 2024 household income ceilings, e.g. € 28,181.07 with 0 dependants, € 44,981.11 with 2, + € 7,044.17 per extra person (2026-2027)
eligibility.residence_requirement: EU citizens: permanent residence right in Belgium or work in Belgium (student jobs do not count), personally or through a parent/partner on the Belgian household composition; non-EU: at least 5 years' residence in Belgium on 31 October 2026, or a parent who is an EU/EEA/Swiss national working in Belgium; refugees: status recognised at least 1 year
other: No study aid from another country
Full-time ('plein exercice') programme; not for doctorate, specialisation master or second degree at the same level
Erasmus/internship stays count with a lease of at least 3 months

items.how_to_apply: Electronic or paper form to the Direction des Allocations d'Études
items.deadline: 1 July to 31 October 2026 for 2026-2027; late applications until 31 January 2027 under conditions
items.stackable: Grant holders pay € 0 minerval; DAE also grants the reduced 'condition modeste' (€ 374) and 'intermédiaire' (€ 835) rates
items.notes: Applies to UCLouvain (Louvain-la-Neuve). A student who comes from abroad only to study normally does not meet the residence/work conditions.

items.name_local: Master Mind Scholarships (Flemish Ministry of Education and Training)
items.name_it: Borse Master Mind del governo fiammingo
items.authority: Flemish Ministry of Education and Training (Study in Flanders)
items.description: Merit scholarship for outstanding international students admitted to a master's in Flanders or Brussels (Flemish institutions): a grant plus a tuition waiver. Candidates are nominated by the host institution (max 20 applications each).

other: New international master's student (60 or 120 ECTS)
Strong academic record (UGent: GPA 3.5/4.0) and good English
Detailed nationality/residence criteria are on a separate Study in Flanders page that was not read
Some places reserved for Japan, Mexico, Palestine and the USA

items.amount: € 10,225 per academic year + tuition waiver (institution may charge the lowest grant-holder rate, € 136.50 in 2026-2027)
items.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to the master's; the programme nominates candidates
items.deadline: 2026-2027 call closed; 2027-2028 modalities under review (UGent: admission application before 1 April)
items.stackable: Not combinable with other Flemish government scholarships, Erasmus+ / Erasmus Mundus, BAEF or Fulbright

items.description: Flemish child benefit, which continues for students; working too much as a student can temporarily end the entitlement.

other: Conditions for a foreign student who comes to Flanders alone were not verified
Secondary sources: kept up to 650 h/year on a student contract or 80 h/month on another contract

items.notes: groeipakket.be refused automated access. The Flemish jobstudent page only confirms that too much student work can end the Groeipakket temporarily; age limit, amounts and residence conditions not verified. Wallonia and Brussels have their own family allowance systems (not researched).

items.authority: De Lijn (Flanders: buses and trams in Leuven, Ghent and the rest of Flanders)
items.description: Youth season ticket for unlimited travel on the De Lijn network for ages 18-24, loaded on a MOBIB card.
items.amount: € 165 for 12 months, € 98 for 3 months, € 40 for 1 month (prices shown on 2026-11-25) + € 10 MOBIB administration fee
items.how_to_apply: Buy online or at De Lijn sales points
items.stackable: Further discounts and preferential rates can lower the price (page does not detail them)
items.notes: The page does not state the year the prices apply to.

items.name_local: Abonnement STIB 18-24 ans Bruxellois / MIVB 18-24 jaar Brusselaar
items.name_it: Abbonamento STIB 18-24 anni per residenti a Bruxelles
items.description: Annual STIB pass for 18-24 year-olds who are 'Bruxellois'; others pay the standard STIB pass.
items.amount: € 12 for 12 months (tariff from 1 February 2026); standard STIB pass € 56/month or € 560/year
items.how_to_apply: STIB sales points / online, on a MOBIB card

interpretations.hypothesis: 'Bruxellois' means domiciled (registered) in one of the 19 communes of the Brussels-Capital Region, so a student registered in Brussels qualifies.
Students not registered in Brussels (e.g. exchange students with Annex 3septies, commuters) pay the standard € 56/month or € 560/year.

items.notes: The tariff decree (Moniteur belge 10.12.2025) does not define 'Bruxellois'; confirm with STIB.

items.description: TEC youth subscription prices could not be read.
items.notes: UCLouvain says under-25s get reduced public transport fares (https://uclouvain.be/en/support/budget).

items.name_local: Belastingvrije grens jobstudenten / seuil d'imposition étudiants jobistes
items.name_it: Soglia di esenzione fiscale per studenti lavoratori
items.authority: Flemish Government information page; FPS Finance (federal income tax)
items.description: Jobstudents pay no income tax unless their annual gross earnings exceed the threshold; they must still file a tax return. Higher earnings can also make parents lose the dependent-child tax benefit.

other: Working only as a student

items.amount: No tax up to € 15,971.43 gross per year (2026)
items.how_to_apply: Automatic via the annual tax return
items.notes: Border students with Annex 33 pay at least 25% non-refundable tax (UGent job service). Federal tax rule, valid in all regions.

items.name_it: Contributi sociali ridotti per lavoro studentesco (650 ore)
items.description: Within the 650-hour yearly quota, student work carries only reduced social contributions for both student and employer; beyond it, normal contributions apply.

other: Student contract; studying is the main activity
Non-EU: within the limits of the residence permit (20 h/week in term if 'labour market limited')

items.amount: Reduced contributions on up to 650 hours per calendar year (since 1 January 2025)
items.how_to_apply: Automatic via the employer's declaration; check remaining hours on My Student@work
items.stackable: Combinable with the jobstudent tax-free threshold
items.notes: Rate not given on the official page; secondary sources (e.g. DLA Piper) give 8.13% in total, 2.71% paid by the student.

items.name_it: Contributo per lo scambio (servizi sociali UGent)
items.description: Allowance for Ghent University students with limited means who go abroad on an exchange or internship; UGent also lists an advance scholarship and a priority scholarship for exchanges outside the Erasmus zone. Outgoing UGent students only.

other: Enrolled degree student at Ghent University going abroad

items.how_to_apply: Via the UGent Social Services student portal
items.notes: Only the overview page was read; the detail page https://www.ugent.be/en/facilities/social-services/exchange-allowance (amount, conditions) was not opened. Incoming exchange students: no host-side Erasmus top-up was found.

items.description: Advice with a student finance adviser and limited financial support for temporary, unforeseen difficulties not caused by the student. KU Leuven states it cannot financially support international students beyond the scholarships on its scholarship website.

eligibility.income_test: Case-by-case; temporary and unforeseen financial difficulty
other: Students are expected to have sufficient means for the whole study period

items.notes: KU Leuven's reduced tuition (beurstarief) follows the Flemish study grant decision (be-fl-studietoelage); exact KU Leuven amounts are in its tuition fee tool (not read).

items.name_it: Tassa ridotta per borsisti e quasi-borsisti (UGent)
items.authority: Ghent University (rates set under Flemish rules)
items.description: Study grant rate if you meet the financial conditions of the Flemish grant; near-study grant rate if your reference income exceeds the grant limit by at most € 4,081 (2026-27). Standard 2026-27 bachelor fee: € 305.40 + € 14.60 per credit (€ 1,181.40 for 60 credits).

eligibility.income_test: Flemish grant financial conditions, or up to € 4,081 above the limit (2026-27)
eligibility.residence_requirement: Belgian, EEA student, or non-EEA student meeting the Flemish grant nationality conditions

items.amount: Grant-holder rate € 139.40 for all credits (2026-2027, UGent bachelor page) instead of € 1,181.40 for 60 credits
items.how_to_apply: Diploma contract: Flemish study grants e-portal; credit contract: UGent Social Services portal
items.stackable: Combines with the Flemish study grant and the UGent allowance for study costs

interpretations.hypothesis: The grant-holder tuition at UGent is € 139.40 for all credits in 2026-2027 (UGent bachelor tuition page).
The lowest Flemish grant-holder tuition is € 136.50 in 2026-2027 (Study in Flanders, Master Mind page).

items.notes: Near-scholarship rate amount not stated on the pages read.

items.name_local: Tegemoetkoming in de studiekosten (UGent Sociale Voorzieningen)
items.name_it: Contributo per i costi di studio (servizi sociali UGent)
items.description: Integrated, case-by-case financial support for financially vulnerable students (study-grant, near-grant or non-grant students after a social-financial assessment); there is no separate housing allowance or rent reduction.

eligibility.income_test: Own resources do not cover study costs; social-financial assessment
eligibility.residence_requirement: Belgian or equivalent under the Flemish study grant nationality conditions
other: Diploma contract of at least 27 credits
Until the first master's degree

items.how_to_apply: After (re)registration, via the Social Services digital student system (about one month processing)
items.stackable: Takes the Flemish study grant into account

items.authority: Vrije Universiteit Brussel – Social, Legal and Financial Support
items.description: Short-term (temporary hardship) or long-term (structural need) interest-free loan for study costs such as tuition, rent or a laptop.

eligibility.income_test: Financial need related to study costs
eligibility.residence_requirement: Must meet one of the Flemish study grant nationality conditions
other: Diploma contract (not credit or exam contract)
Initial programme; advanced master's also eligible for the loan

items.how_to_apply: Short-term: online form at loans.vub.be, contract via DocuSign; long-term: e-mail the signed form (available from September)
items.stackable: Part of VUB's support alongside the Flemish grant and reduced tuition
items.notes: Short-term loans are repaid monthly (min € 50/month); long-term repayment starts two years after leaving VUB. VUB also offers emergency support open to international and exchange students meeting academic conditions (https://www.vub.be/en/studying-vub/practical-info-for-students/how-much-does-studying-cost/financial-support).

items.name_it: Tassa ridotta per borsisti e quasi-borsisti (VUB)
items.description: Full Flemish grant holders pay the scholarship rate automatically; students who meet the nationality and financial conditions but not the age or educational ones can still get the scholarship rate; slightly-above-limit incomes get the near-scholarship rate. Applying for the Flemish grant gives a provisional scholarship rate until the decision.

eligibility.income_test: Flemish grant financial conditions (near-rate: income slightly above the limit)
other: Not for advanced master's, postgraduate, PhD or exam contracts

items.how_to_apply: Apply for the Flemish study grant; credit-contract students apply to VUB with tax and household documents
items.deadline: If no decision by 1 May, the full fee is invoiced and refunded later
items.stackable: Linked to the Flemish study grant
items.notes: VUB page gives no 2026-27 amounts; VUB cost page gives a general tuition range of € 1,116–5,320/year.

items.authority: UCLouvain Student Support Service; FWB Direction des Allocations d'Études
items.description: FWB rates 2026-2027: € 0 for grant holders, € 374 'condition modeste', € 835 'intermédiaire', € 1,194 full. If the FWB does not help, UCLouvain can grant its own social rate of € 374 after an individual assessment.

eligibility.income_test: UCLouvain social rate 2026-27 ceilings: € 36,181.07 (0 dependants) to € 74,652.44 (5), + € 7,044.17 per extra person
eligibility.residence_requirement: UCLouvain social rate: Belgian, or EU national with an employment link in Belgium (student jobs do not count)

items.how_to_apply: FWB rates: apply to the DAE; UCLouvain social rate: Student Support Service form for your campus
items.stackable: FWB grant holders automatically get € 0 minerval
items.notes: Treatment of non-EU nationals under the UCLouvain social rate is not stated (nationality set to EU/EEA/Swiss for that reason; Swiss inclusion not explicit).

items.authority: UCLouvain Student Support Service / Accommodation Service
items.description: Flat-rate monthly rent reduction for students in financial difficulty living in accommodation managed by UCLouvain.

eligibility.income_test: Assessment of own or household income
other: First or second cycle, towards a first university degree
Living in UCLouvain-managed housing

items.how_to_apply: Download the rent reduction form, send it with the required documents
items.deadline: 15 May for the coming academic year (15 May–31 August only within availability)
items.notes: 'Assimilated' is not defined on the page.

items.description: Direct financial support for non-EU students is limited; UCLouvain offers priority for student jobs, coverage of some exceptional medical costs not covered by the health fund, and a refurbished PC under conditions. EU students (or those treated like Belgians) can see a social worker.
items.notes: Bank-guarantee deposits for the visa are handled by UCLouvain's International Relations Office (amount not stated).
